correctness.summary: Brahmagupta reduces the cyclic area to a constrained four-variable product. Complete interior critical-point classification gives the exact minimum below q=4/3; an explicit boundary family proves zero infimum above it. A direct factorization yields the sharp reverse stability constant 12.

limitations: Only nondegenerate convex cyclic Euclidean quadrilaterals are covered.
For q >= 4/3 the lower value is a limiting infimum and is not attained in the nondegenerate class.
No lower-area bound is claimed for arbitrary noncyclic flexible quadrilaterals.
The upper-product counterpart and the opposite sharp deficit inequality are prior work and are not novelty claims.
Older symmetric-polynomial or geometric-inequality literature may contain an equivalent formulation.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Giugiuc--Oai--Altintas (2018) already covers the complementary maximum-product problem and the opposite sharp deficit inequality, which are excluded from novelty. Targeted searches did not locate the exact minimum-area profile, q=4/3 lower-envelope transition, or P^2-16K <= 12V. Equivalent older symmetric-polynomial formulations remain a residual risk.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The theorem determines exactly when side variance forces positive cyclic area, classifies the sharp minimizers, locates the degeneracy threshold, and completes the known one-sided stability estimate with a best reverse constant.
